messages:
jill_customer: Hey team — our production traffic that should be pinned to Dedicated eu-west-1 is routing to hosted in us-east and we got a big billing surprise. Latency went from ~75ms to 420ms and customer complained. Any idea? :frowning:
sara_support: Ugh. Can you paste a few request IDs and the dedicated pool name? Also which SDK/version?
jill_customer: project: redwood-payments, pool: eu-west-1-reserve-42, sample req ids: r-8c1a, r-8c1b, r-8c1e between 2024-11-12T14:12:00Z and 2024-11-12T14:22:00Z. Using JS SDK 1.6.2 pinned to region eu-west-1 in config.
max_infra: I pulled the routing logs for pool eu-west-1-reserve-42 — I see requests matching those IDs but with route decision="hosted-fallback" and region_selected="us-east-1". Hostnames show hosted-worker-xx.
alex_sre: Did the pool report being out of capacity and trigger overflow? Check pool_capacity_free and fallback policy.
max_infra: Pool free slots show 0 at 14:11:50 and autoscale kicked, but there are also a lot of short-lived fallbacks earlier at 14:08 where free slots > 0. Suggests misrouting, not pure capacity.
sara_support: Could be auth token or header causing client to be classified as us-east. Any custom headers or region hints in token?
jill_customer: We set REDWOOD_REGION env on the host to eu-west-1. No custom headers set intentionally.
max_infra: I inspected the request headers for r-8c1a. Found an old client that injects a deprecated header: "X-Client-Region: us-east-1". Our smart-router gives that header precedence in certain code paths — we recently merged a compat patch.
deploybot: deploy: infra/smart-router v2.14.7 → v2.15.0 at 2024-11-12T13:59:02Z :rotating_light:
alex_sre: That deploy aligns with the timestamp. If the compat patch treats X-Client-Region as authoritative, that could override pool pinning in edge cases.
max_infra: Here's the raw header snapshot for r-8c1a:
```
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci... (redacted)
X-Client-Region: us-east-1
X-Request-Id: r-8c1a
X-Redwood-Project: redwood-payments
```
I also decoded the token and noticed it contains a claim region_hint=us-east-1 (old SDK bug included env var in token).
jill_customer: Oh wow — one of our deploys still had REDWOOD_REGION=us-east-1 in a batch worker image. That explains the token claim. How do we fix existing routing and billing?
sara_support: Short term: we can patch the routing policy for your project to prefer dedicated pins strictly (turn off header-based override) and retroactively mark those request ids as dedicated for billing. Liza, can billing do an adjustment if the platform misrouted?
liza_billing: We can open an investigation and issue a credit if Redwood routing caused hosted execution. Need list of request ids + timestamps and the user's account id. We'll start provisional credit once infra confirms misroute.
max_infra: Mitigation steps I recommend now:
1) Revoke the affected tokens (rotate API keys) and redeploy worker with correct REDWOOD_REGION.
2) Temporarily set project routing_policy: "strict_pin": true (we can push from infra console).
3) Blacklist the deprecated header parsing in smart-router config until we ship a safer version.
4) Gather full request traces and hand over to billing.

Repro steps to confirm locally:
```
# simulates bad client
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <old-token-with-region-claim>" -H "X-Client-Region: us-east-1" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Project: redwood-payments" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
```
You should see route decision in response headers: `X-Redwood-Route: hosted-fallback`

To force correct routing as a test until you rotate tokens:
```
# force region header that router respects
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <new-token>" -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Project: redwood-payments" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
```
Will return `X-Redwood-Route: dedicated` if pinned correctly.

max_infra: I pushed a temp patch to your project: strict_pin=true at 2024-11-12T15:02:00Z. That should stop new spillovers. Please rotate tokens and confirm.
tim_dedicated: I also checked the eu-west-1 pool health — no node crashes, normal CPU. Autoscaler did spike but capacity was enough for the traffic bursts. This is definitely header/token misclassification.
jill_customer: Thanks — rotating keys now and redeploying. I'll paste new tokens when done. :heavy_check_mark:
sara_support: Once you confirm rotated tokens, we'll revert strict_pin and roll the header-parse blacklist to global if tests pass.
alex_sre: Long-term: we'll update the router to prefer explicit project pin > token claim > deprecated headers, and add a metric to alert on cross-region execution rate for pinned projects. Filing ticket INFRA-7865.
max_infra: For billing handoff — I exported the affected request ids and traces to /shared/support/redwood-payments-20241112.csv and gave Liza access.
liza_billing: Got it, I started a case. Will follow up with provisional credit and then final after infra audit.
jill_customer: Confirmed new tokens and redeploy completed at 2024-11-12T15:30:10Z. Traffic now routes to dedicated and p95 latency back to ~80ms. Thanks all. :tada:
sara_support: Great — I'll keep the case open until billing finalizes credit. If anything else pops up ping me. :eyes:
deploybot: canary deploy rollback queued for infra/smart-router v2.15.0 at 2024-11-12T16:00:00Z (pending approvals)
alex_sre: We'll proceed with rollback once we have confirmation from security that token rotation was complete.
max_infra: Closing investigation notes: root cause = deprecated header + old token claim + compat change in v2.15.0 router. Impact = hosted execution of pinned requests for subset of users, transient latency and billing exposure. Remediations applied.
jill_customer: Very relieved. Appreciate the quick response.
